lines.say: Five thousand dollars of software, sold abroad, for every person in one country.
This is software and IT exports, per person, since 2005.
In 2005, Israel already sells six hundred seventy five dollars a head. Britain, two fifty.
By 2015, Israel is at nineteen hundred dollars a person.
Saudi Arabia sells oil. Its software exports? Sixty one dollars a person.
Turkey, sixty two. Egypt, fifteen. Jordan, four.
America has Silicon Valley, but it is huge. Two hundred sixty four dollars per American.
Britain, eight hundred sixty four. Germany, six sixty.
Chips too: thirty seven percent of Israel's factory exports are high tech.
Should Israel bet even more on tech? Tell me in the comments.
So how much code does one Israeli sell the world?
Five thousand one hundred eighty dollars.

caption_en:
Oil, gas, or code? One country sells the world something else.

Software and IT (ICT service) exports per person, 2024, current US$ (World Bank exports / population):
Israel $5,180
UK $864
UAE $757
Germany $660
USA $264
Turkey $62
Saudi Arabia $61
Lebanon $24 (2023, latest)
Egypt $15
Jordan $4
Syria, Iran: no data

2005: Israel $675, UK $250. High-technology goods are 37.2% of Israel's manufactured exports (UK 29.2%, USA 24.3%, Turkey 5.1%, Saudi Arabia 0.5%), 2024.
Per person figures favour small countries, and big economies sell far more in total.

Sources: World Bank, World Development Indicators: BX.GSR.CCIS.CD (ICT service exports, BoP), SP.POP.TOTL, TX.VAL.TECH.MF.ZS, 2005 to 2024. The animation interpolates between years.
Photos: Intel Haifa (xiquinhosilva, CC BY 2.0), Khurais oil facility (Planet Labs, CC BY-SA 4.0), Matam Haifa (Zvi Roger, CC BY 3.0), via Wikimedia Commons.

caption_he: ייצוא תוכנה ושירותי IT לנפש, 2024 (הבנק העולמי): ישראל 5,180 דולר, בריטניה 864, ארה"ב 264, סעודיה 61. 37% מהייצוא התעשייתי של ישראל הוא היי טק.
